primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Tangier disease due to ABCA1 loss of function
mechanism: ABCA1 transfers cellular cholesterol and phospholipids to apolipoprotein A-I, initiating nascent HDL formation and promoting cholesterol efflux from macrophages and other cells. Biallelic ABCA1 loss markedly lowers HDL and causes cholesteryl-ester accumulation in reticuloendothelial tissues.
vignette: A 12-year-old boy has enlarged yellow-orange tonsils, hepatosplenomegaly, and a peripheral neuropathy. His plasma HDL cholesterol is nearly undetectable. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in ABCA1.
lead: Which of the following cellular processes is most directly impaired in this patient?
correct: Efflux of cellular cholesterol and phospholipids to apolipoprotein A-I during nascent HDL formation
distractors: Receptor-mediated uptake of LDL particles by hepatocytes
Transfer of triglycerides onto apolipoprotein B in the endoplasmic reticulum
Export of plant sterols from enterocytes back into the intestinal lumen
Trafficking of unesterified cholesterol out of late endosomes and lysosomes
distractor_notes: LDL-receptor defects cause familial hypercholesterolemia and do not explain the extremely low HDL and orange tonsils of Tangier disease.
Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein is required for ApoB-containing lipoprotein assembly; its deficiency causes abetalipoproteinemia.
ABCG5/ABCG8 mediate intestinal and hepatobiliary plant-sterol efflux; their loss causes sitosterolemia rather than Tangier disease.
NPC1/NPC2 defects impair lysosomal cholesterol trafficking and cause Niemann-Pick type C, a different lipid-storage disorder.
key_expl: Tangier disease is caused by biallelic ABCA1 loss of function. ABCA1 moves cholesterol and phospholipids from cells onto apo A-I, generating nascent HDL and permitting cellular cholesterol efflux. Loss of this pathway causes extremely low HDL and cholesterol accumulation in tonsils, spleen, liver, and other reticuloendothelial tissues.
objective: Link Tangier disease to failure of ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux onto apo A-I and impaired nascent HDL formation.
